verses.1: Should we still choose ourselves again? Or should we not do so, as some have done with their letters to you?
verses.2: This letter is for you. It is written in our hearts, and it has been seen and recognized by all people.
verses.3: It is clear that this is a letter from Christ, delivered to us by the Holy Spirit. It was written not with ink, but with the breath of God living in it. It isn’t written on paper or stone, but rather in the hearts and souls of people.
verses.4: We believe this, through Christ, in relation to God.
verses.5: Not that we are capable of doing anything on our own, but rather, our ability comes from God.
verses.6: He who established us as prophets of a new covenant – not through writing, but through the Spirit. For writing destroys things, while the Spirit gives life.
verses.7: But if the rites of death were established in writing, and inscribed on stones, then it would be impossible for the sons of Israel to approach Moses’ face because of the glory that his face possessed.
verses.8: How, then, will the service of the Spirit be more honorable?
verses.9: For if the service of judgment brings glory, then the service of justice brings even more glory.
verses.10: And indeed, one will not be able to appreciate the glory that is present in this place, because of the excessive glory involved.
verses.11: For if what is being destroyed is done out of fame, then the thing that remains in fame is even more important.
verses.12: Having such a hope, we will be blessed with many blessings.
verses.13: And not in the same way that Moses covered his face, so as not to reveal his identity to the sons of Israel at the end of the destruction.
verses.14: But their meaning has changed over time. Up to today, this covering that protects the ancient covenant remains unbroken, as it is said that it is abolished in Christ.
verses.15: But until today, Moses’ teachings will still be remembered in their hearts.
verses.16: But if it returns to its owner, then the cover will be removed.
verses.17: And the “Lord’s breath” is freedom. And this “Lord’s breath” represents freedom itself.
verses.18: We all, with a changed appearance, can reflect the glory of the Lord. We will be transformed from glory into another form of glory, just as we were transformed by the Spirit of the Lord.
